page_title: Frame Player — a video player for Windows and macOS

summary.name: Frame Player
summary.one_liner: Free, open-source video player for Windows and macOS built on libmpv, with torrent streaming, TV casting without re-encoding, and synchronized group watching.
use_cases: stream a torrent while it downloads
cast a local video to a Chromecast or DLNA TV
watch a series with friends in sync
play MKV, HEVC, HDR or Dolby Vision files
download subtitles automatically by file hash
remove black bars from a video
resume an unfinished episode or film
summary.what_it_does: Plays local files, folders, links, magnet links, .torrent files and RSS feeds in one window, using libmpv so most mpv-supported formats play. It streams torrents while they download, prioritising pieces near the playhead, and seeding is off by default. It casts to Chromecast, DLNA and, from a Mac, AirPlay TVs, sending the file unchanged when the TV supports it and otherwise remuxing it. A shared six-character code keeps several viewers on the same timeline, correcting drift by adjusting playback speed. It also searches OpenSubtitles by file hash, can auto-crop black bars, and resumes unfinished videos after a restart.
notable: Torrent streaming with playback starting before the download finishes
Casts to Chromecast, DLNA and AirPlay TVs, remuxing without re-encoding when possible
Watch-together rooms joined by a six-character code, syncing by speed rather than seeking
Built on libmpv, the engine behind mpv and IINA
caveats: Not available on Linux, and Intel Macs are not supported (Apple Silicon only)
Windows builds are unsigned and stop once at SmartScreen
The Torznab indexer search sends search queries through the project's proxy and has an off switch
